annotations.text:
What disagreed, before decision 104.

The zone and account panels set rows in the HUD's 12-point mono capitals; settings spoke the menu face at 17, sentence case; the ship panel was a third anatomy with two heads stacked and its own row height.

Grounds sat at four opacities, rules at four alphas, rows were inset by two different measures and stood at two different heights, and the log-in card was the one surface with no glass behind it at all.

None of it was decided; each was written by whoever wrote the page. All of it is one thing now.

The language, in one breath.

Everything is a panel; a panel is rows; a row is one shape. One glass, one edge, one head, one band, one wash pair, one breathing key.

The menu speaks in the menu face at 17, sentence case; it reads in the mono at 14; it quotes names raw. Capitals belong to the HUD and to the small labels, which are the mono at 12.

A row's right end is what the row does: opens, reads, steps, fills, switches, or walks. Six ends spell every menu in the game, and a row is 44 tall on every one of them.

A panel is as tall as what it holds, standing on the bottom margin it slid out of, and eases to a new height when a stack changes what is on top. Every number is the shipped one.

What shipped, and what changed after it did.

Chris picked the menu's voice, so every row in the game speaks it: the AltVoice board is the road not taken, kept as the record of the choice.

Then he used it, and decision 105 corrected six things these boards now carry. The wash is flat: the brighter left edge is what a selection looks like against a lit rule, which the drawer had and a panel does not. The head lights, because it is a control. A switch takes enter and space. A panel is as tall as what it holds rather than the height of the window. A pointer lights every row, not the ones that had been thought about. And shrapnel reads the fragments a rung throws rather than the rung, because it is the one add-on whose magnitude is another weapon.

A reading is 14 points, not the 12 these boards first captioned, and there is no dense 36-point row: no surface wanted one.

A confirm is still a card. The room-change question has two equal answers and no commit, and a question that costs a pilot their hold should not be the size of the screen.
